This vignette demonstrates msprimeR's demographic, ancestry-model, rate-map,
mutation-model, replicate and pedigree interfaces. msprimeR is an independent
R mirror of upstream msprime, not an official upstream release. Please cite
the canonical msprime publication; `citation("msprimeR")` provides the full
reference.

## Structured demography

Population IDs are zero-based; population names can be used instead. Migration
rates are backward-time rates, matching the coalescent lineage direction.

```{r}
demography <- Demography$new()
demography$add_population(name = "north", initial_size = 5000, growth_rate = 0.002)
demography$add_population(name = "south", initial_size = 3500)
demography$add_population(name = "ancestor", initial_size = 10000)
demography$set_symmetric_migration_rate(c("north", "south"), 1e-4)
demography$add_population_parameters_change(
  time = 200, population = "south", initial_size = 2500, growth_rate = 0)
demography$add_population_split(
  time = 1000, derived = c("north", "south"), ancestral = "ancestor")
demography$sort_events()
demography
```

Use the debugger to inspect epochs and lineage locations:

```{r}
debugger <- demography$debug()
debugger$epoch_start_time
debugger$population_size_history
debugger$possible_lineage_locations(samples = c("north", "south"))
```

A demes model can be resolved from an R list and converted to a Demography:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("yaml", quietly = TRUE)}
demes_yaml <- "
time_units: generations
demes:
  - name: ancestor
    epochs: [{end_time: 1000, start_size: 10000}]
  - name: north
    ancestors: [ancestor]
    epochs: [{start_size: 5000}]
  - name: south
    ancestors: [ancestor]
    epochs: [{start_size: 3500}]
"
graph <- resolve_demes(yaml::yaml.load(demes_yaml))
deme_model <- Demography$from_demes(graph)
names(deme_model)
```

## Rate maps and ancestry models

A RateMap describes changing rates along the sequence. NaN intervals denote
unknown map regions; missing flanks are trimmed from the returned sequence.

```{r}
recombination <- RateMap$new(
  position = c(0, 2e5, 5e5, 1e6),
  rate = c(1e-8, 3e-8, 1e-8))
recombination$mean_rate
```

An ancestry simulation may run a sequence of models:

```{r}
ts <- sim_ancestry(
  samples = list(SampleSet(4, "north"), SampleSet(4, "south")),
  demography = demography,
  sequence_length = 1e6,
  recombination_rate = recombination,
  model = list(DiscreteTimeWrightFisher(duration = 20), StandardCoalescent()),
  random_seed = 21)
ts
```

Other models include Hudson's coalescent (default), SMC, SMC', SMC(k), Beta
and Dirac multiple-merger coalescents, selective sweeps, and fixed pedigrees.

## Mutation models and replicates

```{r}
mts <- sim_mutations(ts, rate = 1e-8, model = HKY(kappa = 2), random_seed = 22)
table(ts_table(mts, "sites")$ancestral_state)
replicates <- sim_ancestry(
  samples = 6, population_size = 1000, sequence_length = 1e5,
  recombination_rate = 1e-8, random_seed = 23, num_replicates = 3)
vapply(replicates, function(x) x$num_trees, numeric(1))
```

## Fixed pedigrees

`PedigreeBuilder` constructs the individual table and paired sample nodes
required by the fixed-pedigree model. Parent references are zero-based and may
refer to individuals added later.

```{r}
pedigree <- PedigreeBuilder$new()
founder_a <- pedigree$add_individual(time = 2)
founder_b <- pedigree$add_individual(time = 2)
pedigree$add_individual(time = 1, parents = c(founder_a, founder_b))
pedigree$add_individual(time = 0, parents = c(2, 2))
pedigree_tables <- pedigree$finalise(sequence_length = 1000)
fixed <- sim_ancestry(
  initial_state = pedigree_tables, model = FixedPedigree(),
  recombination_rate = 1e-4, random_seed = 24)
fixed
```

Pedigrees can be exchanged as text with `write_pedigree()` and
`parse_pedigree()`. Tree traversal and population-genetic statistics are
provided by tskitR; ancestral node dating is provided by tsdateR. See the
`interoperability` vignette for the `.trees` handoffs.
